message.content:
READ-ONLY IDOR/authorization audit of server actions in /opt/nxeon (Next.js, Prisma). Check "use server" action files for IDOR / missing-ownership / missing-admin-gate bugs.

For EACH exported server action taking an id string from the untrusted client, determine whether it checks the resource belongs to the caller (customer actions: `row.userId === user.id` after requireUser) OR whether admin-only actions gate with `requireAdmin()`/`requireStaff()`/`requireArea()` at the START. Flag:
1. IDOR: `db.MODEL.findUnique/update/delete({where:{id}})` where the only predicate is client-supplied id, reachable by a normal customer, no ownership check.
2. Missing admin gate: an action that mutates admin/global data but never calls requireAdmin/requireStaff/requireArea — a normal customer could invoke it.
3. Mass-assignment: spreading untrusted input into prisma create/update that could set role/isAdmin/userId/balance/status.

These files are a mix of customer + admin surfaces. For board/chat/coldemail note whether they're admin-only (the board and coldemail are admin tools per the app). An admin tool with NO admin gate that mutates by client id is a HIGH finding.

Files to audit (read each fully):
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-board.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-chat.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-coldemail.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-coldemail-inbox.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-improvements.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-staff.ts

/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-nodes.ts

/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-reviews.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-calendar.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-gameplans.ts

For each real finding: exact file:line, action name, model, who can call it, attacker impact, one-line fix. Rank CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM. If a file is clean, say so in one line. Verify helpers before calling anything clean. Return findings as final message text.

content.text:
I have read all 15 target files and verified every authorization helper they rely on (`requireAdmin`, `requireArea`, `requireUser`, `realUser`, `requireStaff` in `lib/auth.ts` + `lib/rbac.ts`, and `resolveMailbox` in `lib/mail/imap.ts`). Here are my findings.

## Summary

No IDOR, missing-admin-gate, or mass-assignment vulnerabilities were found. Every exported server action across all 15 files either gates on an admin/staff area at its very first statement, or (for the two customer-facing surfaces) scopes the resource to the authenticated caller before touching it. This code appears to have already been hardened — several files carry explicit comments documenting previously-fixed authorization defects.

## Helper verification (the trust anchors)

- `requireAdmin()` (auth.ts:229) — throws `FORBIDDEN` unless `role === "ADMIN"`. Solid.
- `requireArea(area)` (rbac.ts:132) — uses `realUser()` (ignores impersonation), `redirect("/dashboard")` for customers, `redirect("/admin")` for wrong-area staff. `redirect()` throws `NEXT_REDIRECT`, which halts the action before any mutation. Area→role map (rbac.ts:24): `platform`/`fleet`/`analytics` = ADMIN-only; `support` = SUPPORT+ADMIN; `billing` = BILLING+ADMIN; `clients` = SUPPORT+ADMIN. Effective gate.
- `requireUser()` (auth.ts:223) — throws `UNAUTHORIZED` if unauthenticated; returns any authenticated user (customer included), so callers must scope by `user.id` themselves.
- `resolveMailbox(addr)` (imap.ts:278) — calls `requireUser()`, then loads only `db.mailbox` rows where `subscription.userId === user.id` (imap.ts:324) and throws "You do not have access to that mailbox" (imap.ts:347) on any address that isn't one of the caller's own. Company-mailbox branch is `isStaff`-gated. Ownership is enforced.

## File-by-file verdict

- **actions-board.ts** — CLEAN. Admin tool; all 24 exports begin with `await requireAdmin()` (e.g. `updateCard`:384, `deleteCard`:422, `moveCard`:398, `runCardStageAction`:510). Mutations by client id are ADMIN-gated, so no customer reachability. Stage pipeline uses a fixed allowlist (no shell injection). Note per instructions: this is admin-only and correctly gated.

Customer-facing, but every export routes through `resolveMailbox(mailboxAddress)`, which enforces caller ownership of the mailbox (verified above). `createEvent`/`createTask` additionally call `assertOwnedCalendar` (204/278). Event/task `id`s are CalDAV hrefs operated through the caller's own authenticated SOGo credential, so per-principal ACL enforces object-level ownership. Mutations are rate-limited (`limitMutations`). No user-owned resource is addressed by client id; no IDOR.

## Notes / non-findings worth recording

- **Mass assignment**: none. The three places that spread into Prisma (`saveReview`, `saveBrand`, node create) all spread a zod-parsed object with a closed field set; none can reach `role`/`isAdmin`/`userId`/`balanceCents`/`status`.
- **Calendar object-level authz** relies on the SOGo CalDAV server's per-principal ACL rather than an explicit `assertOwnedCalendar` on the delete/update-by-href paths (`updateEvent`:215, `deleteEvent`:239, `setTaskCompleted`:289, `deleteTask`:307). This is the platform's intended model (the credential itself is user-scoped), so it is not a Prisma IDOR — but if you want defense-in-depth, adding an `assertOwnedCalendar(calendarUrlOf(id))` check before those writes would harden against a hypothetical CalDAV-ACL misconfiguration. Low priority, not a current vulnerability.

No CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM findings to rank — all 15 files are clean under the IDOR / missing-gate / mass-assignment criteria.
